messages:
sara: quick thread - proposing a lightweight proxy preflight to assert residency constraints before accepting writes in active-active. idea is preflight checks + "demote-to-local" policy when remote owner region rejects.
mike: +1 on preflight but worried about latency spike on every write. is this async or sync?
sara: sync for first-write-in-session or first-write-after-lease-swap. then cache result per-tenant for TTL. keep critical path small.
juan: what's the exact signal? a single RPC from edge proxy to owner-region control plane?
sara: yes: /v1/tenancy/{t}/residency-check -> {allowed_regions:[..], policy: "local-only"|"global-allowed"}. response cached by edge.
anna: how do we handle split-brain window where ownership moved but cache still says allowed? fallbacks?
mike: on 409 or residency-reject, proxy should attempt demote flow: 1) return RESIDENCY_MISMATCH header + hint 2) enqueue a background notify to owner region to re-evaluate 3) if tenant policy allows, accept write locally as "demoted-local" with audit tag.
juan: demoted-local seems risky for compliance. need explicit per-tenant opt-in. default should be reject.
sara: agreed. propose tenant flag: residency_failover: ["reject","demote_local","queue_for_owner"]. default: reject for high-risk tenants.
legal-bot: note: any automated cross-region acceptance for EU data must have documented consent. keep demote_local opt-in only after signed contract flag.
anna: ok. telemetry: record preflight_latency, preflight_cache_hit, demote_events, residency_rejects. want these in per-tenant dashboards.
mike: implementation notes: preflight should be UDP-ish? jk :) but seriously keep headers small: X-Redwood-Residency-Token + cached verdict. consider bloom filter cache for allowed regions to reduce control-plane lookups.
juan: SSR (size) concerns: if we cache per-tenant, thousands of tenants could blow memory on edge. TTL + LRU and eviction prioritized by traffic.
sara: rollout plan: 1) admin-only opt-in tenants 2) proxy preflight + cache 3) expose demote flag, default reject 4) collect telemetry 5) evaluate egress cost and legal sign-offs.
mike: pseudo: 

GET /v1/tenancy/:t/residency-check -> 200 {policy:"reject", allowed:["eu"], ttl:3600}
edge_cache.set(key, verdict, ttl)
if cache.miss: call control-plane
if verdict.reject and tenant.default==demote_local && signature_ok: accept with tag "demoted_local" else return 403 + header X-Residency-Hint:owner=eu

juan: can we piggyback this on existing routing header X-Redwood-Residency? would minimize SDK changes.
sara: yes, but need control-plane API anyway. SDKs shouldn't change for reads. only error codes documented: RESIDENCY_VIOLATION + hint.
legal-bot: also record KMS key origin when demoted_local events occur. audits will want that.
anna: long-term refactor: merge tenancy residency metadata and cluster-lease table into single fast lookup index so preflight is O(1) and we avoid control-plane fanout.
mike: agree. reviewers? I'll take perf and cache design. juan take security/compliance. anna take telemetry. sara will author RFC patch.
sara: thanks all. I'll open RFC follow-up and include sample control-plane schema, proxy cache eviction rules, and per-tenant flags. will ping reviewers once draft is ready.
